body: The US Justice Department has asked a federal judge in California to let the government keep a Chinese-registered Gulfstream G550 that federal agents seized in Alaska in May 2026. Prosecutors say the US-built business jet flew from Beijing to Tehran without the required US authorization and spent six days in Iran.

The October 28 civil forfeiture complaint identifies the aircraft as a 2012 Gulfstream G550, registration B-8259, registered to Deer Jet (Beijing) Co., Ltd. According to the filing, the jet flew to Tehran on December 13, 2024, and stayed there until it returned to Beijing on December 19. The six days the Gulfstream spent in Tehran are central to the government's case: at the time, a US Treasury Department general license allowed certain foreign-registered civil aircraft to visit Iran for up to 72 hours, provided they met the other conditions of the license. Prosecutors say the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control never approved a longer stay for B-8259.

The flight itself also required US approval, prosecutors allege. Because the Gulfstream was built in the United States, flying it from China to Iran technically counted as a reexport under US export control laws. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security never issued a license for the trip, according to the complaint. Federal agents seized the Gulfstream under a warrant when it landed in Anchorage on May 24, 2026, more than a year after it returned from Tehran. By the time prosecutors filed the case, the jet was in FBI custody in Virginia. The Justice Department asked the court to give anyone with a claim to the aircraft an opportunity to contest the forfeiture before the judge decides who gets to keep it. If the court grants forfeiture, the US government could sell the Gulfstream or keep it for official use; the complaint does not say what it intends to do with the jet.
en.summary: The US Justice Department has asked a federal judge in California to let the government keep a Chinese-registered Gulfstream G550 seized in Anchorage in May; prosecutors say the jet flew from Beijing to Tehran in December 2024 and stayed six days without US export-control approval, beyond the Treasury's 72-hour general license.
en.title: US seeks to keep Chinese-registered Gulfstream G550 seized after trip to Iran

body: 美國司法部已請求加州聯邦法官，准許政府保有聯邦幹員2026年5月在阿拉斯加安克拉治扣押的一架中國註冊灣流G550公務機。檢方表示，這架美國製造的公務機在未取得必要美國許可的情況下，自北京飛往德黑蘭，並在伊朗停留6天。

10月28日提出的民事沒收訴狀指出，該機為2012年出廠的灣流G550，註冊編號B-8259，登記於Deer Jet (Beijing) Co., Ltd.名下；訴狀稱，該機2024年12月13日飛抵德黑蘭，12月19日才返回北京。檢方指出，6天的停留時間是本案關鍵：當時美國財政部通用許可僅允許特定外國註冊民用航空器在伊朗停留最多72小時，財政部外國資產管制辦公室（OFAC）從未批准B-8259停留更久。

檢方另稱，由於該機在美國製造，自中國飛往伊朗在技術上屬於美國出口管制法下的再出口，須取得美國許可，但商務部工業與安全局（BIS）從未就此行核發許可。聯邦幹員於2026年5月24日持搜索票，在該機降落安克拉治時將其扣押，此時距離該機自德黑蘭返回已逾一年；提出訴狀時，該機由聯邦調查局（FBI）保管於維吉尼亞州。司法部請求法院在法官裁定前，給予任何對該機有權利主張者提出異議的機會；若法院准予沒收，美國政府可出售該機或留作公務使用，訴狀未說明政府打算如何處置。
zh.summary: 美國司法部請求加州聯邦法官准許政府保有5月在安克拉治扣押的中國註冊灣流G550；檢方指該機2024年12月自北京飛往德黑蘭並停留6天，未取得美國出口管制許可，且超出財政部72小時通用許可期限。
zh.title: 美司法部要求法院准許沒收中國註冊灣流G550，涉未經許可飛往伊朗
